config.note: Composed: british-ds-1 for the other passes; filler-words from british-jev-1 (jev-1.13.0, thinking off).

findings.note: 'realization' names the act of realizing, and it is carried by the empty verb phrase 'had come to'.

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: 'Decision' names the act of deciding, and the clause's verb is the empty 'was made'.
'Evaluation' names the act of evaluating, carried by the empty verb 'carried out'.

The clause is passive and no by-phrase names who does the clearing. The preceding sentence names the contracts as specifying the rule, not as the party performing the work, so the actor remains unstated.

findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus, I
findings.note: The subject 'I' arrives seventeen words into the sentence, after an introductory clause and a modifier. This exceeds the ten-word threshold.

findings.quote: Municipal snow contracts in our city
findings.note: The paragraph was describing the narrator's morning walk and arrival; this sentence introduces an unrelated municipal snow-clearing policy. The next sentence returns to the narrator's realization, as if the policy sentence were not there.
'picturesque' appears twice within two sentences; the first occurrence is in 'a picturesque row of Victorian houses'.
Doubled pair: 'plain and simple' says one thing twice.

findings.quote: the top of the hill that February
findings.note: This paragraph presupposes the hill and the first winter, which the paragraph beginning "The first winter was very hard." introduces later. "the hill" and "that February" therefore have no antecedent where they stand.
'Review' is an action noun; the verb 'conduct' carries no meaning of its own, burying the act of reviewing.
'determination' buries the verb 'determine' behind the empty verb 'makes'.
Three consecutive sentences open with the same words, 'The board'. A run of three sentences.

findings.quote: Given the results of the pilot and what both teams told us in the May retrospective,
findings.note: The main subject, "I", arrives after nineteen words of introductory material.

findings.quote: It was decided in 2023 that all changes would go through this process
findings.note: The draft never names who decided that all changes would go through this process. It is a decision the paragraph's argument rests on, and no actor appears in the clause or nearby sentences.
The draft never says who raised the concerns, and the surrounding sentences name no one. The reader cannot tell whether this was the teams, the leads, or management.
The draft never says who should note this; the impersonal construction hides the person making the claim.
Doubled pair: 'full and complete' says one thing twice.
Stock image; the draft does not say what the constraint actually consists of or how it would bind.

Restatement. The pilot outcomes in the preceding sentence, both teams cut their median wait from six days to under one and neither shipped a change that had to be rolled back, already carry the assessment.

findings.quote: As noted above, the board would still review every high-risk change, and nothing in this proposal would change that.
findings.note: Restatement. The concession that the board would continue to meet, but only for changes that touch billing, authentication or customer data already makes this point.

findings.quote: Oversight would remain in place for the changes where it matters most, and that point should not be lost.
findings.note: Restatement. This repeats the board-would-still-review-high-risk-changes point made in the same paragraph and earlier in the memo.

"The pilot" and "both teams" have no antecedent at this point; they are supplied only by the later paragraph beginning "In March and April, the Payments and Search teams ran a pilot", so the reader cannot identify either reference where it stands.

findings.quote: In the weeks after the water went down and the loss adjuster had come round to photograph each and every room,
findings.note: Twenty-two words precede the subject 'Ellen'.
'Undertaking' names the act of undertaking, carried by the empty verb 'given'.
'Assessment' names the act of assessing, carried by the empty verb 'carry out'.
The noun 'decision' carries the action while the verb 'made' does little work; the decision is what follows. A form of the root verb 'decide' exists.

findings.quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued
findings.note: The draft never says who failed to issue the warnings, though the omission is the point of the sentence.
No promiser is named in the clause or the surrounding sentences, and the broken promise is the cost the sentence is about.
'sodden' repeats within two sentences; the first occurrence is in 'the smell of sodden flour stayed in the building for weeks.'
'Whole' appears twice in two sentences; the first occurrence is in 'the whole street' at the start of the paragraph.
'Affected' appears twice within two sentences; the first is in the paragraph's opening sentence. The second use in 'the flood affected the people of the street' repeats the same verb.
Doubled pair: 'each and every' says the same thing twice.
The previous sentence is about the bakery being the heart of the street; 'a wave of support' is a new element, and its link to the crowd's reaction comes only after the subject.

The opening names 'the election', which nothing earlier in the paragraph or draft mentions; the previous sentences were about the flood wall's history. The link to the flood wall arrives only after the comma.

findings.quote: Gluten development depends on water temperature
findings.note: The sentence opens on a general fact about gluten development, which the reader cannot connect to the previous sentence about Tom driving for flour. It is an aside: the next sentence, 'By the end of March she was selling', continues from the sentence before it.

findings.quote: the beating heart of Quay Street
findings.note: A stock image standing in for a claim about the bakery's importance that the draft never specifies. The figure supplies no picture beyond the assertion itself.

findings.quote: lit a fire under the council
findings.note: A stock image used in place of the draft's unspecified account of what the support actually caused the council to do.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways. Some lost stock and some lost income, and some lost things that are harder to put a price on.
findings.note: Restatement: the previous paragraphs already show the flood's varied effects on Quay Street residents.

findings.quote: It is difficult to overstate how much the flood affected the people of the street, and it would be impossible to describe every way in which their lives were changed by it.
findings.note: Restatement: repeats the point already made in the preceding sentence about the flood's many effects on Quay Street people.

findings.quote: She rang her son Tom, who lives two streets up the hill.
findings.note: The flood-morning account begun in the opening paragraph is dropped for the insurance paragraph and resumes here, leaving related material on either side of an unrelated paragraph.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways.
findings.note: Repeats the street-wide-impact point already made in the paragraph beginning 'It was obviously a shock to the whole street', including the second sentence's claim that the extent of the effect cannot be overstated.
'Observation' is the action buried in the noun; the verb 'made' carries it.
'There was' carries the action noun 'expectation', burying the verb 'expect'.
'Decision' is the action noun and 'made' is the empty verb carrying it.
The clause hides who would make the decision; the sentence names only the committee that decided to make one, not the actor of this action.

findings.quote: It is a feeling that is familiar. It is a feeling that recurs.
findings.note: Two consecutive sentences are built on the same template, 'It is a feeling that is ...', with the second repeating the opening of the first.
The word 'feeling' appears three times in three sentences, beginning with the first sentence's 'the feeling that nothing had been accomplished'.

findings.quote: It was decided by the committee that a decision would be made regarding the proposal.
findings.note: Repeats the earlier paragraph beginning "It was decided by the committee thxt x determination would be made regarding the proposal." The two paragraphs carry the same content, so this one adds nothing.

findings.quote: There was an expectation that a resolution would be arrived at.
findings.note: Repeats the earlier paragraph beginning "There was an expectation that". No new information is added.

findings.quote: Some of us left the room with the feeling that nothing had been accomplished.
findings.note: Repeats the earlier paragraph beginning "Some of us left the room with the feeling that". The paragraph restates a point the draft has already made.
